title: The integral normalized compact-support compositor square for two coefficient fields
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l distinct from its characteristic, composable separated finite-type morphisms f:X→Y and g:Y→Z of finite-type D.k-schemes, and compactifications cf,cg,cfg [def-weil-finite-field-fiber; def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties; def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let E,L be finite extensions of Q_l and ι:E→L a Q_l-algebra embedding [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Let AE and AL be natural integral compact-support compositors for these three compactifications over E and L, satisfying SfIntegralCompositionSpec [def-zl-field-shriek-composition-normalization]. Let bf,bg,bfg be the three integral scalar comparison natural isomorphisms satisfying SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action]. Writing T_W for the completed integral coefficient extension on W and F_c,E for the integral compact-support functor [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action], every integral constructible K satisfies T_Z(AE_K);bfg_K = bg_(F_cf,E K);F_cg,L(bf_K);AL_(T_X K). This is an equality in the integral constructible category; no rationalization, algebraic closure, stage systems or localization hypotheses occur.

Construction: inverse open adjunct of the proper/open restriction map, outer proper pushforward, and proper/open compositors; independence of choices.

proof.text: Choose a compatible compactification tower dominating cf,cg,cfg. Expand AE and AL by SfIntegralCompositionSpec. The scalar mates preserve the open unit, proper counit and pullback compositor defining Lambda; transposing identifies the scalar square of its inverse open adjunct Gamma. Whisker with outer proper and open functors and paste proper/open compositor squares, using scalar tensor associativity. On constant-coefficient strict towers the central pasted square is already the declared PurStrictScalar.scalar_compactification_composition; transport it through the fixed constant/completed comparisons.

The normalized refinement comparisons commute with the prescribed scalar mates. Cancel their inverse pairs and use projection-normalized qcqs realization to identify the resulting square with the recorded integral functors. The supplied beta finite tensor-unit equations identify reductions of the two composites. Apply the constructible mapping-limit argument of integralConstructibleReductionHom: shifted Hom groups into restricted finite reductions are finite, so the Milnor lim-one term vanishes and reduction detects equality for these constructible maps. Extend the separated-scheme finiteness calculation to the present qcqs schemes by a finite affine cover: intersections are quasicompact separated finite-type schemes, and boundedness makes the Cech spectral sequence finite in the fixed Hom degree. This supplies the required injectivity without asserting faithfulness of finite evaluation on arbitrary derived maps.

theorem sfIntegralComposition_coefficient_comm
    (AE : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf E ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg E ≅
      sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cfg E)
    (AL : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf L ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg L ≅
      sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cfg L)
    (hAE : SfIntegralCompositionSpec l E D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf cg cfg AE)
    (hAL : SfIntegralCompositionSpec l L D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf cg cfg AL)
    (bf : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf E ⋙
        sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι Y ≅
      sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι X ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf L)
    (bg : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg E ⋙
        sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι Z ≅
      sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι Y ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg L)
    (bfg : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cfg E ⋙
        sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι Z ≅
      sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
          E L ι X ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cfg L)
    (hbf : SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cf E L ι bf)
    (hbg : SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg E L ι bg)
    (hbfg : SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cfg
      E L ι bfg)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) :
    (sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime))
        E L ι Z).map (AE.hom.app K) ≫ bfg.hom.app K =
      bg.hom.app
          ((sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl)
            cf E).obj K) ≫
        (sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (coefficientPrimeUnit l D hl) cg L).map
          (bf.hom.app K) ≫
        AL.hom.app
          ((sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
            (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι X).obj K)
